edges.description: The disease allele sits in the ELMO domain, which is the domain that carries the GAP activity, and recombinant protein bearing it has no measurable activity against ARL2.

The step from a lost GAP activity to a disordered actin cytoskeleton is the weakest link in this chain and is curated as such. What is measured is that ELMOD3 localises with actin and that the disease allele abolishes that localisation, and separately that the knockout cochlea has less F-actin. The intermediate - which ARF-family GTPase acts on which actin regulator - is the paper's own speculation.
The node is a localisation rather than a lesion; the edge says the stereocilium is where the missing activity is missing from.

Phalloidin signal is much weaker throughout the knockout cochlea, most markedly in hair cells, and stereocilia formation and maturation are already delayed at postnatal day 1.
edges.limitations: The mouse is a complete null and the human allele is a missense change that leaves the protein in place; a null and a catalytically dead protein need not have the same cellular consequence, particularly for a protein that also has a localisation function. No human cochlear tissue has been examined, so the actin phenotype is assumed rather than shown in the disease.

edges.description: Inner hair cell stereocilia are significantly shortened at two months and by five months show noticeable degeneration, with a few inner hair cells lacking bundles entirely.
edges.limitations: The human bundle has never been examined, so the correspondence is between a mouse structural phenotype and a human audiogram. The direction is also the opposite of the paralogue Elmod1 knockout, in which stereocilia elongate, so the bundle consequence of losing an ELMOD protein is not generic and should not be transferred between them.

edges.description: The mouse goes deaf, which is the right outcome, but on a completely different schedule from the humans: thresholds are normal at one month, shift from two months, and worsen to five months.
edges.limitations: The affected members of family PKDF468 are deaf before they learn to speak, to a severe-to-profound degree, while the knockout has normal hearing for its first two months and then develops a moderate loss. The mouse also has a purely sensorineural phenotype and the humans have mixed audiograms. Both are recorded as an open human-model mismatch.

nodes.description: The cochlea can no longer turn sound into a neural signal at normal levels. In the mouse this is progressive and measured as auditory brainstem response threshold shifts from two months of age; in the affected members of family PKDF468 it is already established before speech acquisition, and it is the sensorineural half of their mixed audiograms.

nodes.description: Two copies of the c.794T>C (p.Leu265Ser) allele, which substitutes serine for a leucine that is conserved across species and that lies inside the ELMO/CED12 domain. The substitution is present in every ELMO-domain-containing isoform of ELMOD3, so it is not escaped by alternative splicing. The protein is still made - what is lost is what the ELMO domain does.

nodes.description: Where the protein is, in rodent inner ear, and the reason the disease is cochlear and not vestibular. ELMOD3 immunoreactivity is in the stereocilia, kinocilia and cuticular plate of developing cochlear hair cells, more intense in inner than in outer hair cells. In the saccule, utricle and ampulla the antibody labels hair cell and supporting cell bodies but not the hair bundles.

nodes.description: A CRISPR/Cas9 null generated by a 277 bp deletion at exon 6, producing a premature stop at residue 149; ELMOD3 protein is undetectable in the homozygous cochlea. This model carries essentially all of the mechanism downstream of the GAP defect in this entry. Heterozygotes have normal thresholds, so it models the recessive entity rather than the dominant one.

No treatment is reported for any member of family PKDF468 and nothing gene-directed exists. Amplification and audiological rehabilitation are curated as the management that the severity and prelingual onset indicate; they substitute external gain for a failing cochlea and do not act on the ELMOD3 mechanism.

In the knockout mouse, inner hair cell stereocilia are significantly shortened by two months - the age at which thresholds first shift - and by five months every inner hair cell shows bundle degeneration, some with no bundle at all. Hair cell bodies themselves are largely preserved, so this is a bundle lesion rather than hair cell death.

nodes.description: ELMOD3 is a GTPase-activating protein for ARL2, an ARF-family GTPase. The p.Leu265Ser protein retains no or almost no activity in vitro. In the mouse cochlea ARL2 protein itself is less abundant when Elmod3 is absent, from postnatal day 7 onwards, so the consequence in tissue is not only a slower GTP-hydrolysis cycle but a smaller ARL2 pool.
